title: TIME JUMP: 00:30 CST, Watch Cleared, Recovery Begins

fields.narration:
It is now 00:30 CST, Saturday, December 12, 2026. The line of storms has moved east of Brennan County. The cold front has come through behind it. Ashford is down to 47 degrees, and a northwest wind is gusting to 40 miles per hour. At 00:20, NWS Paducah cleared Brennan County from the Particularly Dangerous Situation Tornado Watch. The county is not under any watch or warning now. For the people in Corwin and the Clarks River parks, the night is far from over. It is cold, it is dark, and many of them have no home to go back to.

The EOC door opens. Deputy EM Director Ray Okafor walks in soaked to the skin and speaks to the room: "We've been at Level 3 since the warning. Give me the room and I'll run it as EOC manager. I need three windshield teams now, for Corwin, the Clarks River parks and Ridgeline, and someone to put all of this into WebEOC."

THIS IS AN EXERCISE.
worldState: Clock: 00:30 CST, Saturday, December 12, 2026. Brennan County was cleared from the PDS Tornado Watch at 00:20 and is under no watch or warning. Ashford: 47°F, northwest wind gusting to 40 mph, rain ending.

Power: Brennan Rural Electric Cooperative's hourly report shows 7,450 members without power, including all of Corwin, Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres. Ashford Municipal Utilities reports 1,900 customers out on two Ashford feeders.

Corwin Wax & Candle: Corwin Fire has found 17 of the 24 missing workers. Nine of them have gone to hospital. Seven are still missing under the collapsed east roof span. The gas meter is shut off, and rescue work goes on under the steel.
Pine Hollow, lot 14: Sheriff Unit 12 reached the overturned home. The mother and both children were brought out alive and taken to hospital.

Spotter Brennan-14 walked into the Clarks River bridge checkpoint at 00:18, unhurt, with a dead radio. Both spotters reported missing earlier, Brennan-14 and Brennan-09, are now accounted for on the SKYWARN net.
Ridgeline Distribution: all 310 workers are accounted for, and four have minor cuts. The north dock doors were blown in and 6 trailers overturned.

Safe rooms: if you ordered them open, 186 people are in the Corwin Community Center and 122 in Ashford Middle School, and many have no home to return to. If you did not, both buildings are still dark and locked, and people are sheltering wherever they can find a roof.

Cell sites serving Corwin, Pine Hollow and the Clarks River corridor are still down. WEA and BrennanAlert texts are not reaching the north end. The county VHF repeater and Channel 6 are still working.
Channel 6 is still on air from the basement backup set with one camera. Sirens N-07 and N-11 are still out of service.
Deputy EM Director Ray Okafor is in the EOC and is offering to take over as EOC manager.

instructorNote: This card moves play from response to recovery. Watch whether the EM Director confirms or declares Level 3 and formally hands EOC manager duties to the Deputy, and whether the room protects the candle plant rescue while starting damage assessment and a two-hour public message cycle.
